Key in a Secret in the imagebuild namespace holding the cloud-config

| Field | Type | Required | Description |

#### `.spec.firstBootSealing`

Declares that every clone of this image seals the listed partitions
to its own vTPM on its first boot (ADR-0088), which is what lets a
`VMClass` with `tpmEnabled: true` use an `Immediate` (pre-installed)
image. Without it that pairing is refused, because the template was
installed before any per-VM vTPM existed (ADR-0048).

For a `Url` source `banlieue-imagebuilder` writes the sealing policy
into the built image itself (`status.firstBootSealing: Built`); for a
`Template` or `BackingFile` source the image must already carry it, and
this field is an operator assertion (`Asserted`). Either way every
clone's `GuestReady` waits for the guest to report each listed
partition sealed. Needs a source image on Kairos v4.4.0 or later.
Honoured unless `banlieue-controller` runs with
`--enable-first-boot-sealing=false`, which refuses a `VirtualMachine`
of this image (`FirstBootSealingDisabled`). Not combinable with
`trustedBoot`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `partitions` | string[] |  | Kairos partition labels to seal on first boot. Defaults to `[COS_PERSISTENT]`. `COS_OEM`, `COS_STATE`, `COS_RECOVERY` and `COS_GRUB` are refused at admission, mirroring Kairos's own refusal. |
| `timeoutSeconds` | integer |  | Seconds from the machine's power-on (its infrastructure `Ready` transition) within which the guest must report every listed partition sealed; after that `GuestReady` is `False` with reason `FirstBootSealingTimeout`. A clone that cannot seal halts in its initramfs and never reports anything, so this is how it is noticed. |

#### `.spec.isoOverlay`

Additional files overlaid onto a built ISO for `Url`-kind vSphere
sources (e.g. a hand-verified `grub.cfg`). Resolved by
`banlieue-imagebuilder` into the kairos-operator `OSArtifact`'s
`spec.volumes[]` + `spec.artifacts.overlayISOVolume` — the same
`auroraboot build-iso --overlay-iso` mechanism a hand-run ISO-build
pipeline would use. See `IsoOverlaySource` and ADR-0022. Ignored for
`cloudImage`-kind builds and non-`Url` sources.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `files` | object[] |  | Explicit key -> ISO-relative-path mapping. At least one entry expected; an empty list is accepted but wires nothing into the `OSArtifact`. |
| `secretRef` | object | Yes | Secret in the imagebuild namespace holding the overlay file contents. |

##### `.spec.isoOverlay.files[]`

Explicit key -> ISO-relative-path mapping. At least one entry expected;
an empty list is accepted but wires nothing into the `OSArtifact`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | string | Yes | Key within the overlay Secret holding this file's content. |
| `path` | string | Yes | Destination path, relative to the ISO root (e.g. `boot/grub2/grub.cfg`). |

##### `.spec.isoOverlay.secretRef`

Secret in the imagebuild namespace holding the overlay file contents.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | Yes |  |

#### `.spec.prelay`

Pre-lay the built image (ADR-0113): `banlieue-imagebuilder` boots the
raw `cloudImage` once, at build time, through the Kairos recovery
reset every clone would otherwise run on its first boot, so each
clone boots straight into the installed system. Only for a `Url`
source built as a `cloudImage`; an `iso` build is refused
(`PrelayNeedsCloudImage`). The pre-lay Job runs the published
`banlieue-prelay` image (`banlieue-imagebuilder --prelay-image`) and
needs `/dev/kvm` on the build node. The published artifact is the pre-laid file, with a
checksum the builder computed after verifying the built file against
the source's `checksum`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `diskSizeGiB` | integer | Yes | The clones' OS disk size, in GiB. `COS_PERSISTENT` fills a disk of this size and does not grow on a larger one, and a smaller one cannot hold the image: give the classes that use this image this disk size (ADR-0113 Decision 4). |

#### `.spec.sources[]`

Per-provider source mappings — one backend binding for this catalog
entry per `providerClass` you intend to schedule VMs onto ("one
name, many backends", see the type-level doc comment above).

`x-kubernetes-list-type: map` keyed on `providerClass`: the API
server rejects a second entry for a `providerClass` that already
has one, rather than leaving it to `find_url_source` /
`find_vsphere_source` to silently pick whichever came first.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `checksum` | string |  | Optional checksum for imported images. Format: `<alg>:<hex>`, e.g. `sha256:9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b...`. Supported algorithms: `sha256`, `sha512`. For a `Url` source, `banlieue-imagebuilder` verifies the built artifact against this value once the build finishes and fails the build closed on mismatch or an unsupported algorithm (ADR-0010, amendment 2026-11-26); it is optional because the build measures the artifact itself. |
| `importFrom` | string |  | Optional source URL. When set, providers that support image import will pull from here if the image isn't already present locally. |
| `kind` | string | Yes | What kind of backend artifact `ref` refers to. Allowed: `Template`, `BackingFile`, `Url`, `OciArtifact`. |
| `providerClass` | string | Yes | Name of the ProviderClass this source applies to. Conventional values: `vsphere`, `proxmox`, `libvirt`. |
| `ref` | string | Yes | Provider-interpreted reference: vsphere + Template: template name e.g. "ubuntu-22.04-cloudinit" proxmox + Template: template VMID e.g. "9000" libvirt + BackingFile: path e.g. "/var/lib/libvirt/images/ubuntu.qcow2" firecracker + OciArtifact: `<repository>@sha256:<manifest digest>` * + Url: ignored; uses `importFrom` |

#### `.spec.template`

How the backend **template** is built from a `Url` source (root
folder, network, disk, CPU / memory / firmware / NIC, force knobs).
Every field is optional and falls back to a built-in default. Only
meaningful for `Url` sources, with one exception: for a vSphere
`Template` source (an existing template banlieue adopts and never
builds) only `rootFolder` is read, to find the template in
`<rootFolder>/<failure-domain>`; every other field is ignored.
Ignored for `BackingFile`. See `VMImageTemplate`, ADR-0020 and
ADR-0104.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cpus` | integer |  | Virtual CPU count of the template (`govc vm.create -c`). When unset, defaults to 2. vSphere-only. |
| `disk` | object |  | Install disk of the template (the clone source's disk). When unset, a thin 100 GiB disk on a pvscsi controller is used. |
| `firmware` | string |  | Firmware for the template (`govc vm.create -firmware`). Reuses the backend-agnostic `Firmware` hint (`bios` / `efi` / `efi-secure`). When unset, defaults to `efi`. vSphere maps `efi-secure` to EFI with secure boot enabled. Allowed: `bios`, `efi`, `efi-secure`, `null`. |
| `forceCreate` | boolean |  | Recreate the template even if one of that name already exists, destroying the existing one first. Threaded as `--force-create`. |
| `forceUpload` | boolean |  | Re-upload the built ISO even if one of that name already exists on the backend, deleting the existing one first (the vСenter datastore file API does not overwrite in place). Threaded as `--force-upload`. |
| `guestId` | string |  | vCenter `guestId` for the template (`govc vm.create -g`, e.g. `rhel9_64Guest`, `ubuntu64Guest`). When unset, it is derived from the VMImage's `osFamily` / `osDistribution` / `osVersion`. vSphere-only. |
| `installMode` | string |  | How the template's install step is driven. See `InstallMode` and ADR-0021 / ADR-0040. Allowed: `immediate`, `deferred`, `manual`. |
| `installTimeoutSeconds` | integer |  | Bound, in seconds, on how long the import Job waits for the unattended Kairos install to finish and the VM to power itself off (`install.poweroff: true` in the cloud-config) before failing the Job. When unset, defaults to 1800 (30 min). See ADR-0021: the golden disk is never rebooted by the build, so this bounds only the (typically 8-12 min) unattended-install window, not a boot cycle. |
| `memoryMib` | integer |  | Memory of the template, in MiB (`govc vm.create -m`). When unset, defaults to 4096. vSphere-only. |
| `network` | object[] |  | The template's network interfaces. Empty means exactly one NIC, using every per-entry default below — the same behavior this field had before it became a list (ADR-0031). vSphere-only. |
| `retainOnDelete` | boolean |  | Keep the per-zone vCenter template(s) this `VMImage` caused to be built when the `VMImage` itself is deleted. When unset (the default), deleting a `VMImage` also destroys every per-zone template it owns — declarative deletion, matching `VirtualMachine`'s own cascade onto its `VSphereMachine` (ADR-0026). Set `true` to opt out — e.g. the template is still referenced by another generation, or its lifecycle is managed by hand outside banlieue. vSphere-only; ignored by any other provider. See ADR-0028. |
| `rootFolder` | string |  | Root vCenter inventory folder (path under the datacenter's VM folder, e.g. `templates/kairos`); created if missing. When unset, the datacenter's VM-folder root is the root. vSphere-only. Read for both `Url` (where the template is created) and `Template` (where the existing template is looked up) sources (ADR-0104). |

##### `.spec.template.disk`

Install disk of the template (the clone source's disk). When unset, a
thin 100 GiB disk on a pvscsi controller is used.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `controller` | string |  | Disk controller type. Defaults to `pvscsi`. Allowed: `pvscsi`, `lsiLogic`, `lsiLogicSas`, `busLogic`. |
| `size` | integer |  | Disk size, in GiB. Defaults to 100 when unset. |
| `type` | string |  | Provisioning hint: `thin` (default), `thick`, or `eagerZeroed`. Reuses the backend-agnostic `DiskProvisioning` shared with `VMClass` / `VSphereMachine`; eager-zeroing is the `eagerZeroed` variant, not a separate flag. Providers honor it on a best-effort basis. Allowed: `thin`, `thick`, `eagerZeroed`. |

##### `.spec.template.network[]`

The template's network interfaces. Empty means exactly one NIC, using
every per-entry default below — the same behavior this field had
before it became a list (ADR-0031). vSphere-only.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `adapter` | string |  | Virtual NIC adapter type for the template (`govc vm.create -net.adapter`). Allowed: `vmxnet3`, `vmxnet2`, `e1000`, `e1000e`. |
| `network` | string |  | Port group this NIC attaches to. When unset, the zone's first reachable network class (ADR-0019) is used. |
| `pciSlot` | integer |  | PCI slot number for this NIC (`ethernetN.pciSlotNumber`). Slot 192 on the first NIC yields a stable `ens192` interface name in the guest. When unset, defaults to `192 + this NIC's index` in `VMImageTemplate.network` — so a template with several NICs and no explicit slots still gets predictable, non-colliding `ens192`/`ens193`/`ens194`/... naming. |

#### `.spec.trustedBoot`

Requests a Trusted Boot (UKI) artifact instead of a classic
kernel+initrd one, for `Url`-kind vSphere sources. Resolved by
`banlieue-imagebuilder` into the kairos-operator `OSArtifact`'s
`spec.artifacts.uki.{iso,keysVolume}` (replacing the plain
`artifacts.iso` request) — the `auroraboot build-uki` mechanism. See
`TrustedBootSource` and ADR-0051. Ignored for `cloudImage`-kind
builds and non-`Url` sources.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `secretRef` | object | Yes | Secret in the imagebuild namespace holding the six files `auroraboot build-uki` requires: `PK.auth`, `KEK.auth`, `db.auth`, `db.key`, `db.pem`, `tpm2-pcr-private.pem`. Generated out-of-band via `auroraboot genkey` — banlieue never generates or manages this key material. |

##### `.spec.trustedBoot.secretRef`

Secret in the imagebuild namespace holding the six files
`auroraboot build-uki` requires: `PK.auth`, `KEK.auth`, `db.auth`,
`db.key`, `db.pem`, `tpm2-pcr-private.pem`. Generated out-of-band via

material.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |

| `name` | string | Yes |  |

### `.status`

Observed availability of a VMImage across the Providers that can serve it.
Maintained by the image controller; read by the scheduler.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `buildArtifact` | object |  | Progress of the shared, provider-agnostic image build for `Url`-kind sources — set exclusively by `banlieue-imagebuilder` (field manager `banlieue.io/imagebuilder`), never by a provider. Typed by `kind` (`cloudImage` for libvirt, `iso` for vSphere). `None` when no `Url` source exists on this `VMImage` or the build hasn't started. See ADR-0010 and ADR-0020. |
| `conditions` | object[] |  | `Ready` is True iff every per-provider entry is ready. |
| `firstBootSealing` | string |  | How banlieue knows an image seals itself on first boot (ADR-0088). Allowed: `Built`, `Asserted`. |
| `observedGeneration` | integer |  |  |
| `perProvider` | object[] |  | Per-Provider readiness. One entry per Provider that supports this image's providerClass and has reconciled at least once. |

#### `.status.buildArtifact`

Progress of the shared, provider-agnostic image build for `Url`-kind
sources — set exclusively by `banlieue-imagebuilder` (field manager
`banlieue.io/imagebuilder`), never by a provider. Typed by `kind`
(`cloudImage` for libvirt, `iso` for vSphere). `None` when no `Url`
source exists on this `VMImage` or the build hasn't started. See
ADR-0010 and ADR-0020.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `checksum` | string |  | `sha256:<hex>` of the built artifact file, measured by `banlieue-imagebuilder` from the file on the artifacts PVC once the build finished (ADR-0010, amendment 2026-11-26); for a pre-laid build, of the pre-laid file (ADR-0113). Set only at phase `Ready`: while it is being measured the phase is `Building` with reason `DigestPending`. When the `Url` source declares a checksum, the build is verified against it first and fails closed on mismatch. Consumers that stream the artifact to a backend MUST verify it against this value and fail closed on mismatch (security review 2026-07-31, SEC-004); a cloud publisher names the published version by it (ADR-0162 Decision 6). |
| `file` | string |  | File name of the artifact within the artifacts PVC (kairos-operator convention: `<osArtifactRef>.raw` for `cloudImage`, `<osArtifactRef>.iso` for `iso`). Populated at phase `Ready`. |
| `firstBootSealingLayer` | boolean |  | Whether this build carries the banlieue-generated first-boot sealing layer (ADR-0088): set when `spec.firstBootSealing` was honoured by the merged cloud-config this artifact was built from. Omitted when false. |
| `kind` | string | Yes | What kind of artifact was built, aligned with kairos-operator's own `OSArtifactKind`. Determines the `file` extension and which provider class consumes it. Allowed: `cloudImage`, `iso`. |
| `message` | string |  | Long human-readable detail, e.g. the `OSArtifact.status.message` on failure. |
| `ociArtifact` | object |  | The same artifact, pushed to an OCI registry for providers that run outside the cluster and cannot mount the artifacts PVC (ADR-0064). Set only when a `cloud-hypervisor` `Url` source exists; `None` otherwise, so installs without a host-resident provider need no registry. |
| `osArtifactRef` | string | Yes | Name of the `OSArtifact` CR `banlieue-imagebuilder` created for this `VMImage` (same namespace as the artifacts PVC below). |
| `osArtifactUid` | string |  | `metadata.uid` of the `OSArtifact` named by `os_artifact_ref`, once observed. Each provider's per-zone import Job sets this as its own `ownerReference` so a rebuilt (deleted-and-recreated) `OSArtifact` garbage-collects the stale Job — and the artifacts PVC mount it holds — instead of the Job outliving it for up to its `ttlSecondsAfterFinished` (ADR-0027). Absent until the `OSArtifact` has actually been observed once. |
| `phase` | string | Yes | Current build phase. Allowed: `Pending`, `Building`, `Ready`, `Failed`. |
| `prelaidDiskSizeGiB` | integer |  | The disk size, in GiB, the artifact was pre-laid for (ADR-0113), when `spec.prelay` was honoured: `file` is then the pre-laid image and `checksum` its digest, computed by the builder. Omitted otherwise. |
| `pvcRef` | object |  | Reference to the PVC kairos-operator created holding the built artifact, once known. Populated no earlier than phase `Building`. |
| `reason` | string |  | Short reason, mirroring the stable-string convention used elsewhere in this status (e.g. `ImagePerProviderStatus.reason`). |

##### `.status.buildArtifact.ociArtifact`

The same artifact, pushed to an OCI registry for providers that run
outside the cluster and cannot mount the artifacts PVC (ADR-0064).
Set only when a `cloud-hypervisor` `Url` source exists; `None`
otherwise, so installs without a host-resident provider need no
registry.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `message` | string |  | Human-readable detail, e.g. why the push failed. |
| `phase` | string | Yes | Current push phase. Allowed: `Pushing`, `Ready`, `Failed`. |
| `reference` | string |  | Digest-pinned reference, `registry/repository@sha256:<hex>`, once the push succeeded. Consumers pull **by this digest** and nothing else: integrity comes from content addressing, so a tag moved after the push cannot change what a host boots. |

##### `.status.buildArtifact.pvcRef`

Reference to the PVC kairos-operator created holding the built artifact,
once known. Populated no earlier than phase `Building`.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | Yes |  |

#### `.status.conditions[]`

`Ready` is True iff every per-provider entry is ready.

Written **only** by `banlieue-controller` (field manager
`banlieue.io/controller`), which is the only component with a
whole-image view. A provider cannot compute "ready everywhere" from
rows it does not own, so it writes its `perProvider` entry and nothing
here (ADR-0015). Merge-keyed on `type`, per Kubernetes convention.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lastTransitionTime` | string | Yes | lastTransitionTime is the last time the condition transitioned from one status to another. This should be when the underlying condition changed. If that is not known, then using the time when the API field changed is acceptable. |
| `message` | string | Yes | message is a human readable message indicating details about the transition. This may be an empty string. |
| `observedGeneration` | integer |  | observedGeneration represents the .metadata.generation that the condition was set based upon. For instance, if .metadata.generation is currently 12, but the .status.conditions[x].observedGeneration is 9, the condition is out of date with respect to the current state of the instance. |
| `reason` | string | Yes | reason contains a programmatic identifier indicating the reason for the condition's last transition. Producers of specific condition types may define expected values and meanings for this field, and whether the values are considered a guaranteed API. The value should be a CamelCase string. This field may not be empty. |
| `status` | string | Yes | status of the condition, one of True, False, Unknown. |
| `type` | string | Yes | type of condition in CamelCase or in foo.example.com/CamelCase. |

#### `.status.perProvider[]`

Per-Provider readiness. One entry per Provider that supports this
image's providerClass and has reconciled at least once.

**Merge-keyed, and it must stay that way (ADR-0015).** Several
providers write this list concurrently, each applying only its own
entry. Without `x-kubernetes-list-type: map` server-side apply treats
the array as atomic — one manager owns the whole thing and `force()`
hands it over wholesale, silently discarding every other provider's
row. That was a real, reproduced bug, not a theoretical one.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ec2` | object |  | `ec2` `Provider`s only: what EC2's `DescribeImages` reports of the AMI in `resolvedRef`, read by the provider so the controller and the scheduler can decide without calling EC2 (roadmap 24 phase E). Unset on every other backend, and until the provider has read the AMI. |
| `message` | string |  | Long human-readable detail. |
| `minOsDiskSizeGiB` | integer |  | Cloud `Provider`s only (ADR-0162 Decision 4, ADR-0160 Decision 4): the smallest OS disk, in GiB, a VM booting the published image may have. Unset until the publish reports it. |
| `providerName` | string | Yes | Name of the Provider. |
| `providerNamespace` | string | Yes | Namespace of the Provider. |
| `ready` | boolean | Yes | True when the image can be used to clone/create a VM on this provider. |
| `reason` | string |  | Short reason if not ready. Stable values from `condition_reasons::IMAGE_*`. |
| `resolvedRef` | string |  | Resolved concrete reference on the backend, for backends with one reference per provider. Proxmox: VMID. Libvirt: path. Azure: the Compute Gallery image version resource ID. Unset for vSphere, whose per-zone references are in `Self::zones` (ADR-0104). |
| `sourceDigest` | string |  | Cloud `Provider`s only (ADR-0162 Decision 4): the digest (`sha256:<hex>`) of the build the published image in `resolvedRef` was made from. Unset for a `Template` source, which banlieue did not publish. |
| `supersededRefs` | string[] |  | Cloud `Provider`s only (ADR-0162 Decision 8): images this `VMImage` published into this `Provider` for an earlier digest, still waiting to be deleted because a machine references them or the delete has not finished. Emptied as each is deleted; recorded here because the provider can read a published image only by its name. |
| `zones` | object[] |  | Per-zone (per-`Provider.status.failureDomains[]`) readiness. Populated by the vSphere provider for both `Url` sources (import progress) and `Template` sources (whether the adopted template exists in each zone's folder, ADR-0104). For `Url`, `ready` means every zone is ready; for `Template` it means at least one zone is, and the scheduler places VMs only in ready zones. Empty for backends without zones (libvirt, Proxmox). |

##### `.status.perProvider[].ec2`

`ec2` `Provider`s only: what EC2's `DescribeImages` reports of the AMI
in `resolvedRef`, read by the provider so the controller and the
scheduler can decide without calling EC2 (roadmap 24 phase E). Unset
on every other backend, and until the provider has read the AMI.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `architecture` | string | Yes | The AMI's architecture: EC2's `x86_64` is `amd64`, `arm64` is `arm64`. An AMI of any other architecture is not made ready. Allowed: `amd64`, `arm64`. |
| `bootMode` | string |  | `bootMode` (`uefi`, `legacy-bios`, `uefi-preferred`); unset when the AMI leaves it to the instance type. |
| `enaSupport` | boolean |  | `enaSupport`. |
| `rootDeviceName` | string | Yes | The AMI's root device name (`/dev/xvda`, `/dev/sda1`): the device the `EC2Machine`'s root volume mapping must name, or EC2 adds the volume beside the AMI's own instead of resizing it. |
| `tpmSupport` | string |  | `tpmSupport`: `v2.0` for an AMI registered for NitroTPM. |

##### `.status.perProvider[].zones[]`

Per-zone (per-`Provider.status.failureDomains[]`) readiness. Populated
by the vSphere provider for both `Url` sources (import progress) and
`Template` sources (whether the adopted template exists in each zone's
folder, ADR-0104). For `Url`, `ready` means every zone is ready; for
`Template` it means at least one zone is, and the scheduler places
VMs only in ready zones. Empty for backends without zones (libvirt,
Proxmox).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `message` | string |  |  |
| `name` | string | Yes | Name of the failure domain, matching `Provider.status.failureDomains[].name`. |
| `ready` | boolean | Yes | True once the template is usable in this zone (import finished for `Url`; template found in the zone's folder for `Template`). |
| `reason` | string |  |  |
| `resolvedRef` | string |  | The template's bare display name within this zone once ready — the value a provider passes to a name-based template lookup. NOT a decorated string (no `[dc]`/folder prefix): the folder lives in `Self::template_folder`, kept separate so a lookup can be built from structured fields instead of parsing this one. |
| `templateFolder` | string |  | The vCenter folder path (relative to the datacenter's VM folder, e.g. `templates/cluster-01`) the template in `Self::resolved_ref` lives in: `<spec.template.rootFolder>/<zone>` for both `Url` imports (ADR-0020 Decision #5) and `Template` sources (ADR-0104). Unset while the zone is not ready. |

## AzureVirtualMachine

**API:** `infrastructure.banlieue.io/v1alpha1` · **Kind:** `AzureVirtualMachine` · **Scope:** Namespaced · **Short names:** `azvm`

AzureVirtualMachine: the concrete, scheduled VM request for Azure.

You normally do not create this by hand: banlieue's controller does,
owned by the `VirtualMachine` it was scheduled from, and the Azure
provider creates the NIC and VM and reports CAPI-shaped status.

**Printer columns** (`kubectl get`):

| Name | Type | JSON path | Priority |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Provider | string | `.spec.providerRef.name` | 0 |
| Zone | string | `.spec.zone` | 0 |
| Size | string | `.spec.size` | 0 |
| Provisioned | boolean | `.status.initialization.provisioned` | 0 |
| State | string | `.status.provisioningState` | 0 |
| Power | string | `.status.observedPowerState` | 0 |
| ProviderID | string | `.spec.providerID` | 1 |
| Age | date | `.metadata.creationTimestamp` | 0 |

### `.spec`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `acceleratedNetworking` | boolean |  | Enable accelerated networking on the NIC. The image must not configure the VF itself (ADR-0163 Decision 3). |
| `desiredPowerState` | string |  | Desired power state, resolved from the parent `VirtualMachine`. `PoweredOff` deallocates the VM, which stops compute billing (ADR-0164 Decision 3). `Suspended` is refused. Allowed: `PoweredOn`, `PoweredOff`, `Suspended`. |
| `failureDomain` | string |  | CAPI contract (optional): failure domain placement, the name of one of the `Provider`'s failure domains (one per availability zone). |
| `imageVersionId` | string | Yes | Resource ID of the Compute Gallery image version to boot, from the `VMImage`'s `azure` source (a hand-published `Template`, ADR-0162 Decision 4). |
| `osDiskSizeGiB` | integer | Yes | OS disk size in GiB, from the `VMClass` (ADR-0160 Decision 4). |
| `osDiskSku` | string | Yes | Managed-disk SKU of the OS disk (`Premium_LRS`, `StandardSSD_LRS`), from the storage class's `sku` target. |
| `providerID` | string |  | CAPI contract: Provider ID for the resulting Node. Format: `azure:///subscriptions/<sub>/resourceGroups/<rg>/providers/Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/<name>`. Set by the provider once the VM exists. |
| `providerRef` | object | Yes | The `Provider` whose connection names the subscription, region and resource group. |
| `size` | string | Yes | VM size (`Standard_D2s_v5`), resolved from the `Provider`'s `instanceSizes` mapping for the `VMClass` (ADR-0160). |
| `subnetId` | string | Yes | Resource ID of the subnet the NIC is created in, from the network class's `subnetId` target for this zone. |
| `trustedLaunch` | boolean |  | Trusted Launch: Secure Boot and a vTPM (ADR-0165). Set from the `VMClass`'s `tpmEnabled`; the image definition must declare Trusted Launch support. |
| `userData` | string |  | Guest bootstrap payload, already resolved and placeholder-substituted by `banlieue-controller` (ADR-0025, ADR-0038). Sent as `customData`; at most 64 KiB. The provider reads no Secret or ConfigMap. |
| `zone` | string | Yes | Availability zone the VM is created in, as the subscription names it (`1`, `2`, `3`). Resolved from the failure domain's `labels.zone`. |

#### `.spec.providerRef`

The `Provider` whose connection names the subscription, region and
resource group.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | Yes | Name of the `Provider`. |
| `namespace` | string |  | Namespace of the `Provider`. Defaults to the referrer's namespace. |

### `.status`

Observed state of an AzureVirtualMachine, shaped to the CAPI v1beta2
InfraMachine status contract. The non-contract fields mean what they mean
on the siblings, so the controller's status mirror treats backends alike.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `addresses` | object[] |  | CAPI contract field (optional): the NIC's private address. No public address in v1. |
| `conditions` | object[] |  | Standard Kubernetes conditions. |
| `createFailures` | integer |  | Consecutive failed creates of this generation: the provider waits `min(5 min * 2^(n - 1), 1 h)` before creating again (ADR-0173 Decision 5). Reset when the VM exists. |
| `failureDomain` | string |  | CAPI contract field (optional): observed failure domain. |
| `guestInstalled` | boolean |  | Sticky: the guest reported ready once (ADR-0163 Decision 1, ADR-0043 Decision 5). |
| `initialization` | object |  | CAPI contract field. |
| `observedGeneration` | integer |  | The `metadata.generation` this status was computed from. |
| `observedPowerState` | string |  | The VM's last observed run state (deallocated reads `PoweredOff`). Allowed: `PoweredOn`, `PoweredOff`, `Suspended`, `null`. |
| `osDiskTagged` | boolean |  | Deprecated, no longer written. v0.6.1 providers set it once they had merged the ownership tags onto the OS disk; ARM already creates the disk with the VM's tags, so the merge is gone (ADR-0173 as amended 2026-11-27). Kept so stored objects stay valid; a value already set is left as it is. |
| `pendingOperation` | object |  | The ARM operation in flight, if any. |
| `provisioningState` | string |  | The VM's ARM `provisioningState` (`Creating`, `Succeeded`, `Failed`). |
| `vmName` | string |  | The VM's resource name, derived from this object's UID. |

#### `.status.addresses[]`

CAPI contract field (optional): the NIC's private address. No public
address in v1.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `address` | string | Yes | The address itself. |
| `type` | string | Yes | Address type. Accepted: Hostname, ExternalIP, InternalIP, ExternalDNS, InternalDNS. Allowed: `Hostname`, `ExternalIP`, `InternalIP`, `ExternalDNS`, `InternalDNS`. |

#### `.status.conditions[]`

Standard Kubernetes conditions.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lastTransitionTime` | string | Yes | lastTransitionTime is the last time the condition transitioned from one status to another. This should be when the underlying condition changed. If that is not known, then using the time when the API field changed is acceptable. |
| `message` | string | Yes | message is a human readable message indicating details about the transition. This may be an empty string. |
| `observedGeneration` | integer |  | observedGeneration represents the .metadata.generation that the condition was set based upon. For instance, if .metadata.generation is currently 12, but the .status.conditions[x].observedGeneration is 9, the condition is out of date with respect to the current state of the instance. |
| `reason` | string | Yes | reason contains a programmatic identifier indicating the reason for the condition's last transition. Producers of specific condition types may define expected values and meanings for this field, and whether the values are considered a guaranteed API. The value should be a CamelCase string. This field may not be empty. |
| `status` | string | Yes | status of the condition, one of True, False, Unknown. |
| `type` | string | Yes | type of condition in CamelCase or in foo.example.com/CamelCase. |

#### `.status.initialization`

CAPI contract field.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `provisioned` | boolean |  | True when the infrastructure provider reports that the resource's infrastructure is fully provisioned. |

#### `.status.pendingOperation`

The ARM operation in flight, if any.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `action` | string | Yes | What the operation is doing. Allowed: `CreateNic`, `CreateVm`, `Start`, `Deallocate`, `DeleteVm`, `DeleteNic`, `DeleteDisk`. |
| `kind` | string | Yes | Which header the URL came from: `AsyncOperation` (`Azure-AsyncOperation`) or `Location`. |
| `url` | string | Yes | The operation URL ARM returned. The provider polls it only when it sits under the ARM endpoint it is configured for. |

## CloudHypervisorMachine

**API:** `infrastructure.banlieue.io/v1alpha1` · **Kind:** `CloudHypervisorMachine` · **Scope:** Namespaced · **Short names:** `chm`

CloudHypervisorMachine — the concrete, scheduled VM request for a Cloud
Hypervisor host.

You normally do not create this by hand: banlieue's controller does, owned
by the `VirtualMachine` it was scheduled from, and the host-resident
provider on the chosen host runs it as a Cloud Hypervisor guest.

**Printer columns** (`kubectl get`):

| Name | Type | JSON path | Priority |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Provider | string | `.spec.providerRef.name` | 0 |
| Provisioned | boolean | `.status.initialization.provisioned` | 0 |
| Power | string | `.status.observedPowerState` | 0 |
| Image | string | `.spec.bootSource.image` | 1 |
| ProviderID | string | `.spec.providerID` | 1 |
| Age | date | `.metadata.creationTimestamp` | 0 |

### `.spec`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bootSource` | object | Yes | Where the OS disk comes from. |
| `cpus` | object | Yes | Virtual CPUs. |
| `desiredPowerState` | string |  | Desired power state, resolved from the parent `VirtualMachine`. Allowed: `PoweredOn`, `PoweredOff`, `Suspended`. |
| `failureDomain` | string |  | CAPI contract (optional): failure domain placement. One host is one failure domain on this backend, as on libvirt. |
| `firstBootSealing` | object |  | First-boot sealing the guest must report before `GuestReady` (ADR-0088, ADR-0112), copied by `banlieue-controller` from the parent `VirtualMachine`'s `VMImage.spec.firstBootSealing` when the class is `tpmEnabled`. The guest reports over its vsock (`sealed=` beside `phase=installed`). `None` for every other machine, which keeps today's `GuestReady` meaning unchanged. |
| `identity` | object |  | The guest identity this machine carries when it is not its own: set by `banlieue-controller` on a move's destination machine to the source's identity (ADR-0127 Decision 6). The provider derives the MAC, tap names, machine directory and EK certificate subject from it instead of from this machine's name and UID, so a moved guest keeps all of them. Absent on every machine that was never the destination of a move. Immutable. |
| `memory` | object | Yes | Guest memory. |
| `moveIn` | object |  | This machine is a move's destination (ADR-0127 Decision 4). Set by `banlieue-controller` at creation; the host provider prepares to receive. |
| `moveOut` | object |  | This machine is a move's source (ADR-0127 Decision 4). Set by `banlieue-controller`; the host provider copies the guest out. |
| `nics` | object[] | Yes | Network interfaces. |
| `osDiskSizeGiB` | integer | Yes | OS disk size in GiB. Required, and grown to before first boot; never shrunk. Must be at least the image's size. |
| `providerID` | string |  | CAPI contract: Provider ID for the resulting Node, if this VM becomes a Kubernetes node. Format: `cloudhypervisor://<provider-name>/<machine-uid>`. Set by the provider once the guest exists. |
| `providerRef` | object | Yes | The `Provider` for the one host that runs this machine (ADR-0060). |
| `storageClass` | string | Yes | Storage class the machine's disks live in. A name the host declares in its local config and publishes on its failure domain; never a path. |
| `tpmEnabled` | boolean |  | Attach a vTPM (swtpm), resolved from the VM's `VMClass.spec.tpmEnabled`. Requires `ChBootSourceKind::InstallMedia` (ADR-0040, ADR-0048, ADR-0065), or an image that seals itself on first boot (`Self::first_boot_sealing`, ADR-0088, ADR-0112). |
| `userData` | string |  | Guest bootstrap payload, already resolved and placeholder-substituted by `banlieue-controller` (ADR-0025, ADR-0038). Rendered into a NoCloud `CIDATA` seed disk; the provider reads no Secret or ConfigMap. |

#### `.spec.bootSource`

Where the OS disk comes from.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `image` | string | Yes | The image in the host's image cache: an installed raw disk for `Image`, the installer ISO for `InstallMedia`. |
| `kind` | string | Yes | Which provisioning shape this machine uses. Allowed: `image`, `installMedia`. |

#### `.spec.cpus`

Virtual CPUs.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `boot` | integer | Yes | vCPUs the guest boots with. |
| `max` | integer |  | Hotplug headroom: the most vCPUs the guest may be resized to. Fixed when the VM is created. `None` means no headroom. |

#### `.spec.firstBootSealing`

First-boot sealing the guest must report before `GuestReady`
(ADR-0088, ADR-0112), copied by `banlieue-controller` from the parent
`VirtualMachine`'s `VMImage.spec.firstBootSealing` when the class is
`tpmEnabled`. The guest reports over its vsock (`sealed=` beside
`phase=installed`). `None` for every other machine, which keeps
today's `GuestReady` meaning unchanged.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `partitions` | string[] |  | Kairos partition labels to seal on first boot. Defaults to `[COS_PERSISTENT]`. `COS_OEM`, `COS_STATE`, `COS_RECOVERY` and `COS_GRUB` are refused at admission, mirroring Kairos's own refusal. |
| `timeoutSeconds` | integer |  | Seconds from the machine's power-on (its infrastructure `Ready` transition) within which the guest must report every listed partition sealed; after that `GuestReady` is `False` with reason `FirstBootSealingTimeout`. A clone that cannot seal halts in its initramfs and never reports anything, so this is how it is noticed. |

#### `.spec.identity`

The guest identity this machine carries when it is not its own: set by
`banlieue-controller` on a move's destination machine to the source's
identity (ADR-0127 Decision 6). The provider derives the MAC, tap names,
machine directory and EK certificate subject from it instead of from
this machine's name and UID, so a moved guest keeps all of them. Absent
on every machine that was never the destination of a move. Immutable.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | Yes | The original machine's name. |
| `uid` | string | Yes | The original machine's UID. |

#### `.spec.memory`

Guest memory.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `hugepages` | boolean |  | Back guest memory with hugepages. The host reports hugepages as their own capacity, since they are reserved rather than allocated on demand. |
| `sizeMiB` | integer | Yes | Guest memory in MiB. |

#### `.spec.moveIn`

This machine is a move's destination (ADR-0127 Decision 4). Set by
`banlieue-controller` at creation; the host provider prepares to receive.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `commit` | boolean |  | Resume the received guest. Written only after the source reported `Sent` and its VMM exited (Decision 5); never written with the source's `abort`. One way. |
| `moveId` | string | Yes | The `VirtualMachineMove` this machine receives. Immutable. |
| `peer` | object |  | The source host, once it has published its certificate. |

##### `.spec.moveIn.peer`

The source host, once it has published its certificate.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `certificate` | string | Yes | The peer's per-move certificate, PEM. |
| `endpoint` | string |  | `host:port` the destination listens on. Set only on the source's `moveOut.peer`: the source connects, the destination listens. |

#### `.spec.moveOut`

This machine is a move's source (ADR-0127 Decision 4). Set by
`banlieue-controller`; the host provider copies the guest out.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `abort` | boolean |  | Give up before commit: resume the guest here (Decision 12). One way; never written once the destination's `commit` is. |
| `cutover` | boolean |  | Pause the guest and send the disk delta and the VMM state. One way. |
| `moveId` | string | Yes | The `VirtualMachineMove` this machine sends. Immutable. |
| `peer` | object |  | The destination host, once it has published its certificate and endpoint. |

##### `.spec.moveOut.peer`

The destination host, once it has published its certificate and
endpoint.

| `attestationSubject` | string |  | The exact certificate subject CN the host's signer sets for this guest: this machine's `metadata.uid`, never a value from the guest (ADR-0146, after ADR-0143 Decision 3). Public and carrying no authorization; mirrored onto the bound claim so mediatore can compute the node entry's parent before the guest boots. Set by the provider only for a host that opted in to attestation; absent otherwise, and when the host withdraws it. |
| `conditions` | object[] |  | Standard Kubernetes conditions. |
| `failureDomain` | string |  | CAPI contract field (optional): observed failure domain. |
| `guestInstalled` | boolean |  | Whether the installed guest has announced itself (ADR-0043). Sticky once true. |
| `hostUid` | integer |  | The unprivileged host uid this machine's units run as (ADR-0063 Decision 3). Recorded so the provider re-adopts a running guest without trusting its own memory. |
| `initialization` | object |  | CAPI contract field. |
| `installMediaDetached` | boolean |  | Whether the installer has been removed, live and for future starts (ADR-0044, ADR-0065 Decision 4). Sticky once true; `None` when there was never an installer. |
| `moveIn` | object |  | The destination side of a move, published by the host provider. |
| `moveOut` | object |  | The source side of a move, published by the host provider. |
| `observedGeneration` | integer |  | The `metadata.generation` this status was computed from. |
| `observedPowerState` | string |  | The VM's last observed run state. Allowed: `PoweredOn`, `PoweredOff`, `Suspended`, `null`. |
| `sealedPartitions` | string[] |  | Partitions the guest has reported sealed, as LUKS containers, on a first-boot sealing machine (ADR-0088, ADR-0112): from the `sealed=` line of its vsock report. **Sticky**: the report is re-sent every boot, and a powered-off machine has not become unsealed. Empty until reported, and on every machine without `spec.firstBootSealing`. Guest-supplied, so it is only ever used to *withhold* `GuestReady`. |
| `tpmAttached` | boolean |  | Whether a vTPM was attached, when `spec.tpmEnabled` is set. |
| `tpmEndorsementCertificates` | string[] |  | PEM EK certificates, validated against this machine (ADR-0045, ADR-0065). |

| `observedGeneration` | integer |  | observedGeneration represents the .metadata.generation that the condition was set based upon. For instance, if .metadata.generation is currently 12, but the .status.conditions[x].observedGeneration is 9, the condition is out of date with respect to the current state of the instance. |
| `reason` | string | Yes | reason contains a programmatic identifier indicating the reason for the condition's last transition. Producers of specific condition types may define expected values and meanings for this field, and whether the values are considered a guaranteed API. The value should be a CamelCase string. This field may not be empty. |
| `status` | string | Yes | status of the condition, one of True, False, Unknown. |

## CloudHypervisorMachineTemplate

**API:** `infrastructure.banlieue.io/v1alpha1` · **Kind:** `CloudHypervisorMachineTemplate` · **Scope:** Namespaced · **Short names:** `chmt`

CloudHypervisorMachineTemplate — a stamped-out CloudHypervisorMachine spec.

CAPI requires an InfraMachineTemplate so a MachineSet or MachineDeployment
can mint identical machines. A spec template, not a disk template: nothing
clones a guest, which is what keeps per-VM vTPMs unique (ADR-0040).

### `.spec`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `template` | object | Yes | The spec stamped into every machine created from this template. |

#### `.spec.template`

The spec stamped into every machine created from this template.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `spec` | object | Yes | The CloudHypervisorMachine spec for machines created from this template. |

##### `.spec.template.spec`

The CloudHypervisorMachine spec for machines created from this template.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bootSource` | object | Yes | Where the OS disk comes from. |
| `cpus` | object | Yes | Virtual CPUs. |
| `desiredPowerState` | string |  | Desired power state, resolved from the parent `VirtualMachine`. Allowed: `PoweredOn`, `PoweredOff`, `Suspended`. |
| `failureDomain` | string |  | CAPI contract (optional): failure domain placement. One host is one failure domain on this backend, as on libvirt. |
| `firstBootSealing` | object |  | First-boot sealing the guest must report before `GuestReady` (ADR-0088, ADR-0112), copied by `banlieue-controller` from the parent `VirtualMachine`'s `VMImage.spec.firstBootSealing` when the class is `tpmEnabled`. The guest reports over its vsock (`sealed=` beside `phase=installed`). `None` for every other machine, which keeps today's `GuestReady` meaning unchanged. |
| `identity` | object |  | The guest identity this machine carries when it is not its own: set by `banlieue-controller` on a move's destination machine to the source's identity (ADR-0127 Decision 6). The provider derives the MAC, tap names, machine directory and EK certificate subject from it instead of from this machine's name and UID, so a moved guest keeps all of them. Absent on every machine that was never the destination of a move. Immutable. |
| `memory` | object | Yes | Guest memory. |
| `moveIn` | object |  | This machine is a move's destination (ADR-0127 Decision 4). Set by `banlieue-controller` at creation; the host provider prepares to receive. |
| `moveOut` | object |  | This machine is a move's source (ADR-0127 Decision 4). Set by `banlieue-controller`; the host provider copies the guest out. |
| `nics` | object[] | Yes | Network interfaces. |
| `osDiskSizeGiB` | integer | Yes | OS disk size in GiB. Required, and grown to before first boot; never shrunk. Must be at least the image's size. |
| `providerID` | string |  | CAPI contract: Provider ID for the resulting Node, if this VM becomes a Kubernetes node. Format: `cloudhypervisor://<provider-name>/<machine-uid>`. Set by the provider once the guest exists. |
| `providerRef` | object | Yes | The `Provider` for the one host that runs this machine (ADR-0060). |
| `storageClass` | string | Yes | Storage class the machine's disks live in. A name the host declares in its local config and publishes on its failure domain; never a path. |
| `tpmEnabled` | boolean |  | Attach a vTPM (swtpm), resolved from the VM's `VMClass.spec.tpmEnabled`. Requires `ChBootSourceKind::InstallMedia` (ADR-0040, ADR-0048, ADR-0065), or an image that seals itself on first boot (`Self::first_boot_sealing`, ADR-0088, ADR-0112). |
| `userData` | string |  | Guest bootstrap payload, already resolved and placeholder-substituted by `banlieue-controller` (ADR-0025, ADR-0038). Rendered into a NoCloud `CIDATA` seed disk; the provider reads no Secret or ConfigMap. |

###### `.spec.template.spec.bootSource`

Where the OS disk comes from.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `image` | string | Yes | The image in the host's image cache: an installed raw disk for `Image`, the installer ISO for `InstallMedia`. |
| `kind` | string | Yes | Which provisioning shape this machine uses. Allowed: `image`, `installMedia`. |

###### `.spec.template.spec.cpus`

Virtual CPUs.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `boot` | integer | Yes | vCPUs the guest boots with. |
| `max` | integer |  | Hotplug headroom: the most vCPUs the guest may be resized to. Fixed when the VM is created. `None` means no headroom. |

###### `.spec.template.spec.firstBootSealing`

First-boot sealing the guest must report before `GuestReady`
(ADR-0088, ADR-0112), copied by `banlieue-controller` from the parent
`VirtualMachine`'s `VMImage.spec.firstBootSealing` when the class is
`tpmEnabled`. The guest reports over its vsock (`sealed=` beside
`phase=installed`). `None` for every other machine, which keeps
today's `GuestReady` meaning unchanged.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `partitions` | string[] |  | Kairos partition labels to seal on first boot. Defaults to `[COS_PERSISTENT]`. `COS_OEM`, `COS_STATE`, `COS_RECOVERY` and `COS_GRUB` are refused at admission, mirroring Kairos's own refusal. |
| `timeoutSeconds` | integer |  | Seconds from the machine's power-on (its infrastructure `Ready` transition) within which the guest must report every listed partition sealed; after that `GuestReady` is `False` with reason `FirstBootSealingTimeout`. A clone that cannot seal halts in its initramfs and never reports anything, so this is how it is noticed. |

###### `.spec.template.spec.identity`

The guest identity this machine carries when it is not its own: set by
`banlieue-controller` on a move's destination machine to the source's
identity (ADR-0127 Decision 6). The provider derives the MAC, tap names,
machine directory and EK certificate subject from it instead of from
this machine's name and UID, so a moved guest keeps all of them. Absent
on every machine that was never the destination of a move. Immutable.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | Yes | The original machine's name. |
| `uid` | string | Yes | The original machine's UID. |

Guest memory.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `sizeMiB` | integer | Yes | Guest memory in MiB. |

This machine is a move's destination (ADR-0127 Decision 4). Set by

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `commit` | boolean |  | Resume the received guest. Written only after the source reported `Sent` and its VMM exited (Decision 5); never written with the source's `abort`. One way. |
| `moveId` | string | Yes | The `VirtualMachineMove` this machine receives. Immutable. |
| `peer` | object |  | The source host, once it has published its certificate. |

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `endpoint` | string |  | `host:port` the destination listens on. Set only on the source's `moveOut.peer`: the source connects, the destination listens. |

This machine is a move's source (ADR-0127 Decision 4). Set by

| `peer` | object |  | The destination host, once it has published its certificate and endpoint. |

The destination host, once it has published its certificate and

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `endpoint` | string |  | `host:port` the destination listens on. Set only on the source's `moveOut.peer`: the source connects, the destination listens. |

## EC2Machine

**API:** `infrastructure.banlieue.io/v1alpha1` · **Kind:** `EC2Machine` · **Scope:** Namespaced · **Short names:** `ec2m`

EC2Machine: the concrete, scheduled instance request for Amazon EC2.

You normally do not create this by hand: banlieue's controller does,
owned by the `VirtualMachine` it was scheduled from, and the EC2 provider
launches the instance and reports CAPI-shaped status.

**Printer columns** (`kubectl get`):

| Name | Type | JSON path | Priority |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Provider | string | `.spec.providerRef.name` | 0 |
| Zone | string | `.spec.zone` | 0 |
| InstanceType | string | `.spec.instanceType` | 0 |
| Provisioned | boolean | `.status.initialization.provisioned` | 0 |
| State | string | `.status.instanceState` | 0 |
| Power | string | `.status.observedPowerState` | 0 |
| ProviderID | string | `.spec.providerID` | 1 |
| Age | date | `.metadata.creationTimestamp` | 0 |

### `.spec`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `desiredPowerState` | string |  | Desired power state, resolved from the parent `VirtualMachine`. `PoweredOff` stops the instance, which stops compute billing (volumes are still billed). `Suspended` is refused. Allowed: `PoweredOn`, `PoweredOff`, `Suspended`. |
| `failureDomain` | string |  | CAPI contract (optional): failure domain placement, the name of one of the `Provider`'s failure domains (one per availability zone). |
| `imageId` | string | Yes | The AMI to launch (`ami-` and 8 or 17 hex digits), from the `VMImage`'s `ec2` source: published by banlieue (ADR-0162 Decision 9) or a hand-published `Template`. When `tpmEnabled` is set, the AMI must be registered with `TpmSupport=v2.0` and `BootMode=uefi` (ADR-0167 Decision 5). |
| `instanceType` | string | Yes | Instance type (`m7i.large`), resolved from the `Provider`'s `instanceSizes` mapping for the `VMClass` (ADR-0160). |
| `iops` | integer |  | Provisioned IOPS: required for `io1` and `io2`, optional for `gp3` (above its baseline), refused for `gp2`. From the storage class's `iops` target. EC2 refuses a value outside the type's range. |
| `kmsKeyId` | string |  | KMS key that encrypts the root volume: a key ID, key ARN, alias name or alias ARN, from the `Provider`'s `connection.ec2.kmsKeyId`. Unset: the account's default EBS key. Volumes are encrypted either way. |
| `providerID` | string |  | CAPI contract: Provider ID for the resulting Node. Format: `aws:///<zone-name>/<instance-id>`, the form the AWS cloud controller manager writes. Set by the provider once the instance exists. |
| `providerRef` | object | Yes | The `Provider` whose connection names the region and the role to assume (ADR-0133: a shared provider serves tenant namespaces). |
| `rootDeviceName` | string |  | The AMI's root device name, which the root volume's block device mapping names. Defaults to `/dev/xvda`, the name banlieue registers its AMIs with. |
| `rootVolumeGiB` | integer | Yes | Root volume size in GiB, from the `VMClass` (ADR-0160 Decision 4). At least the AMI's snapshot size, which EC2 enforces. |
| `securityGroupIds` | string[] | Yes | Security groups of the primary network interface, from the network class's `securityGroupIds` target. At least one. |
| `subnetId` | string | Yes | Subnet the primary network interface is created in, from the network class's `subnetId` target for this zone. No public IP is assigned. |
| `throughput` | integer |  | Throughput in MiB/s, `gp3` only, from the storage class's `throughput` target. EC2 refuses a value outside the type's range. |
| `tpmEnabled` | boolean |  | NitroTPM: the instance gets a TPM 2.0 (ADR-0167). Set from the `VMClass`'s `tpmEnabled`; the AMI must be registered with `TpmSupport=v2.0` and the instance type must support NitroTPM. |
| `userData` | string |  | Guest bootstrap payload, already resolved and placeholder-substituted by `banlieue-controller` (ADR-0025, ADR-0038). Sent as instance user data; at most 16,384 bytes before encoding. The provider reads no Secret or ConfigMap. IMDS is disabled once the guest is ready, so the guest reads it only during its first boot (ADR-0174 Decision 3). |
| `volumeType` | string |  | EBS volume type of the root volume, from the storage class's `volumeType` target. Defaults to `gp3`. Allowed: `gp3`, `gp2`, `io1`, `io2`. |
| `zone` | string | Yes | Availability zone **name** the instance is launched in, as the account names it (`ca-central-1a`). Resolved from the failure domain's `labels.zone`; the zone ID is reported in status (ADR-0158 Decision 3). |

#### `.spec.providerRef`

The `Provider` whose connection names the region and the role to
assume (ADR-0133: a shared provider serves tenant namespaces).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | Yes | Name of the `Provider`. |
| `namespace` | string |  | Namespace of the `Provider`. Defaults to the referrer's namespace. |

### `.status`

Observed state of an EC2Machine, shaped to the CAPI v1beta2 InfraMachine
status contract. The non-contract fields mean what they mean on the
siblings, so the controller's status mirror treats backends alike.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `addresses` | object[] |  | CAPI contract field (optional): the primary private IPv4 address (`InternalIP`) and the instance's private DNS name (`InternalDNS`). No public or Elastic IP in v1. |
| `conditions` | object[] |  | Standard Kubernetes conditions. |
| `createFailures` | integer |  | Consecutive failed creates of this generation: the provider waits `min(5 min * 2^(n - 1), 1 h)` before creating again (ADR-0173 Decision 5). Reset when the instance exists. |
| `failureDomain` | string |  | CAPI contract field (optional): observed failure domain. |
| `guestInstalled` | boolean |  | Sticky: the guest reported ready once on the serial console (ADR-0175, ADR-0043 Decision 5). |
| `imdsDisabled` | boolean |  | Sticky: the provider turned the instance metadata endpoint off after the guest reported ready (ADR-0174 Decision 3). Never turned back on automatically. |
| `initialization` | object |  | CAPI contract field. |
| `instanceId` | string |  | The instance ID (`i-...`), once `RunInstances` returned it or the provider adopted the instance by its ownership tag. |
| `instanceState` | string |  | The instance's EC2 state name (`pending`, `running`, `stopping`, `stopped`, `shutting-down`, `terminated`). |
| `observedGeneration` | integer |  | The `metadata.generation` this status was computed from. |
| `observedPowerState` | string |  | The instance's last observed run state (`stopped` reads `PoweredOff`). Allowed: `PoweredOn`, `PoweredOff`, `Suspended`, `null`. |
| `tpmEndorsementPublicKeys` | string[] |  | The NitroTPM's endorsement key public keys, PEM `SubjectPublicKeyInfo` (RSA-2048 and ECC P-384), read host-side by the provider with `GetInstanceTpmEkPub` once the instance runs (ADR-0167 Decision 1). Never read from the guest. Empty unless `tpmEnabled`. banlieue publishes these and vouches for nothing: the source is the EC2 API its own identity called. |
| `zoneId` | string |  | The zone **ID** (`cac1-az1`) of `spec.zone` in this account: zone names differ per account, IDs do not, so two accounts compare by ID (ADR-0158 Decision 3). |

#### `.status.addresses[]`

CAPI contract field (optional): the primary private IPv4 address
(`InternalIP`) and the instance's private DNS name (`InternalDNS`).
No public or Elastic IP in v1.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `address` | string | Yes | The address itself. |
| `type` | string | Yes | Address type. Accepted: Hostname, ExternalIP, InternalIP, ExternalDNS, InternalDNS. Allowed: `Hostname`, `ExternalIP`, `InternalIP`, `ExternalDNS`, `InternalDNS`. |

#### `.status.conditions[]`

Standard Kubernetes conditions.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lastTransitionTime` | string | Yes | lastTransitionTime is the last time the condition transitioned from one status to another. This should be when the underlying condition changed. If that is not known, then using the time when the API field changed is acceptable. |
| `message` | string | Yes | message is a human readable message indicating details about the transition. This may be an empty string. |
| `observedGeneration` | integer |  | observedGeneration represents the .metadata.generation that the condition was set based upon. For instance, if .metadata.generation is currently 12, but the .status.conditions[x].observedGeneration is 9, the condition is out of date with respect to the current state of the instance. |
| `reason` | string | Yes | reason contains a programmatic identifier indicating the reason for the condition's last transition. Producers of specific condition types may define expected values and meanings for this field, and whether the values are considered a guaranteed API. The value should be a CamelCase string. This field may not be empty. |
| `status` | string | Yes | status of the condition, one of True, False, Unknown. |
| `type` | string | Yes | type of condition in CamelCase or in foo.example.com/CamelCase. |

CAPI contract field.

## EC2MachineTemplate

**API:** `infrastructure.banlieue.io/v1alpha1` · **Kind:** `EC2MachineTemplate` · **Scope:** Namespaced · **Short names:** `ec2mt`

EC2MachineTemplate: a stamped-out EC2Machine spec.

CAPI requires an InfraMachineTemplate so a MachineSet or MachineDeployment
can mint identical machines. banlieue ships it for CAPI compatibility;
standalone VirtualMachine users do not need it.

### `.spec`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `template` | object | Yes | The spec stamped into every machine created from this template. |

#### `.spec.template`

The spec stamped into every machine created from this template.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `spec` | object | Yes | The EC2Machine spec for machines created from this template. |

##### `.spec.template.spec`

The EC2Machine spec for machines created from this template.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `desiredPowerState` | string |  | Desired power state, resolved from the parent `VirtualMachine`. `PoweredOff` stops the instance, which stops compute billing (volumes are still billed). `Suspended` is refused. Allowed: `PoweredOn`, `PoweredOff`, `Suspended`. |
| `failureDomain` | string |  | CAPI contract (optional): failure domain placement, the name of one of the `Provider`'s failure domains (one per availability zone). |
| `imageId` | string | Yes | The AMI to launch (`ami-` and 8 or 17 hex digits), from the `VMImage`'s `ec2` source: published by banlieue (ADR-0162 Decision 9) or a hand-published `Template`. When `tpmEnabled` is set, the AMI must be registered with `TpmSupport=v2.0` and `BootMode=uefi` (ADR-0167 Decision 5). |
| `instanceType` | string | Yes | Instance type (`m7i.large`), resolved from the `Provider`'s `instanceSizes` mapping for the `VMClass` (ADR-0160). |
| `iops` | integer |  | Provisioned IOPS: required for `io1` and `io2`, optional for `gp3` (above its baseline), refused for `gp2`. From the storage class's `iops` target. EC2 refuses a value outside the type's range. |
| `kmsKeyId` | string |  | KMS key that encrypts the root volume: a key ID, key ARN, alias name or alias ARN, from the `Provider`'s `connection.ec2.kmsKeyId`. Unset: the account's default EBS key. Volumes are encrypted either way. |
| `providerID` | string |  | CAPI contract: Provider ID for the resulting Node. Format: `aws:///<zone-name>/<instance-id>`, the form the AWS cloud controller manager writes. Set by the provider once the instance exists. |
| `providerRef` | object | Yes | The `Provider` whose connection names the region and the role to assume (ADR-0133: a shared provider serves tenant namespaces). |
| `rootDeviceName` | string |  | The AMI's root device name, which the root volume's block device mapping names. Defaults to `/dev/xvda`, the name banlieue registers its AMIs with. |
| `rootVolumeGiB` | integer | Yes | Root volume size in GiB, from the `VMClass` (ADR-0160 Decision 4). At least the AMI's snapshot size, which EC2 enforces. |
| `securityGroupIds` | string[] | Yes | Security groups of the primary network interface, from the network class's `securityGroupIds` target. At least one. |
| `subnetId` | string | Yes | Subnet the primary network interface is created in, from the network class's `subnetId` target for this zone. No public IP is assigned. |
| `throughput` | integer |  | Throughput in MiB/s, `gp3` only, from the storage class's `throughput` target. EC2 refuses a value outside the type's range. |
| `tpmEnabled` | boolean |  | NitroTPM: the instance gets a TPM 2.0 (ADR-0167). Set from the `VMClass`'s `tpmEnabled`; the AMI must be registered with `TpmSupport=v2.0` and the instance type must support NitroTPM. |
| `userData` | string |  | Guest bootstrap payload, already resolved and placeholder-substituted by `banlieue-controller` (ADR-0025, ADR-0038). Sent as instance user data; at most 16,384 bytes before encoding. The provider reads no Secret or ConfigMap. IMDS is disabled once the guest is ready, so the guest reads it only during its first boot (ADR-0174 Decision 3). |
| `volumeType` | string |  | EBS volume type of the root volume, from the storage class's `volumeType` target. Defaults to `gp3`. Allowed: `gp3`, `gp2`, `io1`, `io2`. |
| `zone` | string | Yes | Availability zone **name** the instance is launched in, as the account names it (`ca-central-1a`). Resolved from the failure domain's `labels.zone`; the zone ID is reported in status (ADR-0158 Decision 3). |

###### `.spec.template.spec.providerRef`

The `Provider` whose connection names the region and the role to
assume (ADR-0133: a shared provider serves tenant namespaces).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | Yes | Name of the `Provider`. |
| `namespace` | string |  | Namespace of the `Provider`. Defaults to the referrer's namespace. |

## FirecrackerMachine

**API:** `infrastructure.banlieue.io/v1alpha1` · **Kind:** `FirecrackerMachine` · **Scope:** Namespaced · **Short names:** `fcm`

FirecrackerMachine: the concrete, scheduled microVM request for a
Firecracker host.

You normally do not create this by hand: banlieue's controller does, owned
by the `VirtualMachine` it was scheduled from, and the host-resident
provider on the chosen host runs it as a Firecracker guest.

**Printer columns** (`kubectl get`):

| Name | Type | JSON path | Priority |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Provider | string | `.spec.providerRef.name` | 0 |
| Provisioned | boolean | `.status.initialization.provisioned` | 0 |
| Power | string | `.status.observedPowerState` | 0 |
| Image | string | `.spec.image` | 1 |
| ProviderID | string | `.spec.providerID` | 1 |
| Age | date | `.metadata.creationTimestamp` | 0 |

### `.spec`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `desiredPowerState` | string |  | Desired power state, resolved from the parent `VirtualMachine`. Allowed: `PoweredOn`, `PoweredOff`, `Suspended`. |
| `failureDomain` | string |  | CAPI contract (optional): failure domain placement. One host is one failure domain on this backend. |
| `image` | string | Yes | The image to boot: `<repository>@sha256:<manifest digest>`, the resolved `ref` of the `VMImage`'s `OciArtifact` source (ADR-0142 Decision 2). The host pulls only a digest in the repository it pins; the cluster says which image, never where images may come from. |
| `memoryMiB` | integer | Yes | Guest memory in MiB. Fixed at boot, and must cover the image's RAM overlay as well as its working set (ADR-0142 Decision 4): the provider refuses a value below the image's declared minimum. |
| `nics` | object[] | Yes | Network interfaces. One tap each, on the host's private bridge for the network class (ADR-0137 Decision 5). |
| `providerID` | string |  | CAPI contract: Provider ID for the resulting Node, if this VM becomes a Kubernetes node. Format: `firecracker://<provider-name>/<machine-uid>`. Set by the provider once the guest exists. |
| `providerRef` | object | Yes | The `Provider` for the one host that runs this machine. Shared-capable from the first commit (ADR-0133): the namespace may name a `Provider` outside the machine's own, which only `banlieue-controller` may set. |
| `userData` | string |  | Guest bootstrap payload, already resolved and placeholder-substituted by `banlieue-controller` (ADR-0025, ADR-0038). Rendered into a NoCloud seed drive, attached read-only second; the provider reads no Secret or ConfigMap (ADR-0137 Decision 4, ADR-0054). |
| `vcpus` | integer | Yes | Virtual CPUs. Fixed at boot: there is no hotplug (ADR-0137 Decision 7), so a `VMClass` change is a `Recreate`. |

#### `.spec.nics[]`

Network interfaces. One tap each, on the host's private bridge for the
network class (ADR-0137 Decision 5).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ipam` | object | Yes | IP address management for this interface. The address and gateway are passed to the guest on its kernel command line (ADR-0137 Decision 5). |
| `macAddress` | string |  | Optional MAC address. The provider derives a stable one from the machine UID otherwise. |
| `name` | string | Yes | Stable NIC name; echoed in status. |
| `networkClass` | string | Yes | Network class: a name the host resolves to one of its bridges. Never a bridge name from the cluster. |

##### `.spec.nics[].ipam`

IP address management for this interface. The address and gateway are
passed to the guest on its kernel command line (ADR-0137 Decision 5).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pool` | object |  | Pool-based IPAM parameters. |
| `static` | object |  | Static IPAM parameters (address, prefix, gateway, nameservers, domain). |

###### `.spec.nics[].ipam.pool`

Pool-based IPAM parameters.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `poolRef` | object | Yes | Typed reference (apiGroup + kind + name + optional namespace). |

Typed reference (apiGroup + kind + name + optional namespace).

Used wherever the referenced kind is pluggable — e.g. IPAM pools, where we

| `kind` | string | Yes |  |
| `name` | string | Yes |  |
| `namespace` | string |  |  |

Static IPAM parameters (address, prefix, gateway, nameservers, domain).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `address` | string | Yes |  |
| `domain` | string |  | DNS domain, used both as a DNS search domain and (by a `VirtualMachine.spec.networkOverrides` consumer, ADR-0024) to build an FQDN as `<vm-name>.<domain>`. |
| `gateway` | string |  |  |
| `nameservers` | string[] |  |  |
| `prefix` | integer | Yes |  |

#### `.spec.providerRef`

The `Provider` for the one host that runs this machine. Shared-capable

| Field | Type | Required | Description |

Public and carrying no authorization; mirrored onto the bound claim so mediatore can compute the node entry's parent before the guest boots. This class has no vTPM, so this replaces the EK certificate as the published attestation fact. |

| `hostUid` | integer |  | The unprivileged host uid this machine's unit runs as (ADR-0063 Decision 3). Recorded so the provider re-adopts a running guest without trusting its own memory. |

| `observedPowerState` | string |  | The VM's last observed run state. Allowed: `PoweredOn`, `PoweredOff`, `Suspended`, `null`. |

For instance, if .metadata.generation is currently 12, but the .status.conditions[x].observedGeneration is 9, the condition is out of date with respect to the current state of the instance. |
| `reason` | string | Yes | reason contains a programmatic identifier indicating the reason for the condition's last transition. Producers of specific condition types may define expected values and meanings for this field, and whether the values are considered a guaranteed API. The value should be a CamelCase string. This field may not be empty. |
| `status` | string | Yes | status of the condition, one of True, False, Unknown. |

## LibvirtMachine

**API:** `infrastructure.banlieue.io/v1alpha1` · **Kind:** `LibvirtMachine` · **Scope:** Namespaced · **Short names:** `lvm`

LibvirtMachine — the concrete, scheduled VM request for a libvirt/KVM host.

You normally do not create this by hand: banlieue's controller does, owned
by the `VirtualMachine` it was scheduled from, and the libvirt provider
reconciles it into a real domain.

**Printer columns** (`kubectl get`):

| Name | Type | JSON path | Priority |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Provider | string | `.spec.providerRef.name` | 0 |
| Provisioned | boolean | `.status.initialization.provisioned` | 0 |
| Power | string | `.status.observedPowerState` | 0 |
| Domain | string | `.spec.domainName` | 1 |
| ProviderID | string | `.spec.providerID` | 1 |
| Age | date | `.metadata.creationTimestamp` | 0 |

### `.spec`

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bootSource` | object | Yes | How this machine's OS disk comes into being. |
| `desiredPowerState` | string |  | Desired power state, resolved from the parent `VirtualMachine`'s `spec.desiredPowerState` (ADR-0024). Allowed: `PoweredOn`, `PoweredOff`, `Suspended`. |
| `disks` | object[] | Yes | Disks. The first is the OS disk; the rest are blank data disks. |
| `domainName` | string | Yes | libvirt domain name. Unique per host, and the handle every domain procedure takes. |
| `failureDomain` | string |  | CAPI contract (optional): failure domain placement. The banlieue scheduler writes the chosen failure domain here. |
| `firmware` | string | Yes | Firmware. EFI requires OVMF on the host; `EfiSecure` additionally requires a `.secboot.fd` variant and pre-enrolled keys. Allowed: `bios`, `efi`, `efi-secure`. |
| `firstBootSealing` | object |  | First-boot sealing the guest must report before `GuestReady` (ADR-0088), copied by `banlieue-controller` from the parent `VirtualMachine`'s `VMImage.spec.firstBootSealing` when the class is `tpmEnabled`. `None` for every other machine, which keeps today's `GuestReady` meaning unchanged. |
| `machineType` | string |  | QEMU machine type (`q35`, `pc`, …). `None` lets libvirt pick its default for the host's architecture, which is the right answer unless an image needs a specific chipset. |
| `memoryMiB` | integer | Yes | Memory in MiB. |
| `network` | object[] | Yes | Network interfaces. |
| `pool` | string | Yes | Storage pool that holds this machine's volumes, resolved from the storage class by the scheduler. |
| `providerID` | string |  | CAPI contract: Provider ID for the resulting Node, if this VM becomes a Kubernetes node. Format: `libvirt://<provider-name>/<domain-uuid>`. Set by the provider controller after the domain is defined. |
| `providerRef` | object | Yes | Reference to the banlieue `Provider` whose connection details describe the target libvirt host. |
| `tpmEnabled` | boolean |  | Attach an emulated TPM 2.0 device (swtpm), resolved from the VM's `VMClass.spec.tpmEnabled` (ADR-0039). |
| `userData` | string |  | Guest bootstrap payload, already resolved from the parent `VirtualMachine`'s `spec.userData` Secret or ConfigMap (ADR-0038) and placeholder-substituted by `banlieue-controller` (ADR-0025). The provider renders it into a NoCloud `cidata` volume — it never reads a Secret or ConfigMap itself. |
| `vcpus` | integer | Yes | Number of virtual CPUs. |

#### `.spec.bootSource`

How this machine's OS disk comes into being.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | string | Yes | Which of the two provisioning shapes this machine uses. Allowed: `backingVolume`, `installMedia`. |
| `volume` | string | Yes | Volume name within `LibvirtMachineSpec::pool`: the backing image for `BackingVolume`, or the installer ISO for `InstallMedia`. |

#### `.spec.disks[]`

Disks. The first is the OS disk; the rest are blank data disks.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bus` | string |  | Controller bus. Allowed: `virtio`, `scsi`, `sata`. |
| `name` | string | Yes | Stable disk name; echoed in status and used to name the volume. |
| `sizeGiB` | integer | Yes | Disk size in GiB. For an overlay OS disk this is a floor — the overlay is created at least this large. |

#### `.spec.firstBootSealing`

First-boot sealing the guest must report before `GuestReady`
(ADR-0088), copied by `banlieue-controller` from the parent
`VirtualMachine`'s `VMImage.spec.firstBootSealing` when the class is
`tpmEnabled`. `None` for every other machine, which keeps today's
`GuestReady` meaning unchanged.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `partitions` | string[] |  | Kairos partition labels to seal on first boot. Defaults to `[COS_PERSISTENT]`. `COS_OEM`, `COS_STATE`, `COS_RECOVERY` and `COS_GRUB` are refused at admission, mirroring Kairos's own refusal. |
| `timeoutSeconds` | integer |  | Seconds from the machine's power-on (its infrastructure `Ready` transition) within which the guest must report every listed partition sealed; after that `GuestReady` is `False` with reason `FirstBootSealingTimeout`. A clone that cannot seal halts in its initramfs and never reports anything, so this is how it is noticed. |

#### `.spec.network[]`

Network interfaces.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ipam` | object | Yes | IP address management for this interface. |
| `macAddress` | string |  | Optional MAC address (otherwise libvirt generates one). |
| `model` | string |  | Device model. `None` means `virtio`, which is what every image banlieue builds expects. |
| `name` | string | Yes | Stable NIC name; echoed in status. |
| `source` | object | Yes | Resolved bridge or libvirt network. |

##### `.spec.network[].ipam`

Observed state of a LibvirtMachine, shaped to the CAPI v1beta2
